$schema_notes.purpose: Machine/LLM-digestible catalog of EasyCrypt proof-assistant tactics, with per-version change notes.
sources: https://github.com/EasyCrypt/refman/blob/main/refman/_sources/tactics/*.rst.txt -- the new Sphinx refman's actual .rst SOURCE files. HIGHEST PRIORITY source: fetched directly per explicit user instruction that source files (.tex/.rst) take priority over compiled PDF/HTML whenever both exist.

https://github.com/EasyCrypt/easycrypt-doc/blob/main/refman/tactics.tex -- LaTeX SOURCE of the older manual's ambient-logic chapter, fetched directly (second-priority source, used for material not yet in the new refman).
https://github.com/EasyCrypt/easycrypt-doc/blob/main/obsolete/userman/br93.tex -- LaTeX SOURCE, older 'user manual', short prose glosses for a few pRHL tactics.
https://github.com/EasyCrypt/easycrypt (source repo; Releases page used for version history: https://github.com/EasyCrypt/easycrypt/releases).
https://www.easycrypt.info/easycrypt-doc/refman.pdf -- compiled PDF (2024-09-27), used only where no source file could be located.

https://www.easycrypt.info/ec-tactics/ -- rendered Pages site of EasyCrypt/ec-tactics, giving an apparently parser-grammar-derived syntax listing for essentially every program-logic tactic, used as a syntax cross-check where the new refman doesn't yet have a page.

confidence_levels.verified_verbatim_rst_source: Content compiled directly from a fetched refman/_sources/tactics/<name>.rst.txt file -- the new manual's actual source. Highest-confidence tier in this file.
confidence_levels.verified_verbatim_tex_source: Content extracted directly from a fetched .tex SOURCE file in easycrypt-doc (tactics.tex for ambient logic; br93.tex for a handful of pRHL tactic glosses).
confidence_levels.verified_grammar: Exact tactic syntax pulled from https://www.easycrypt.info/ec-tactics/, an apparent parser-grammar dump. Precise on syntax; prose semantics alongside it are a best-effort summary (see summarized_semantics) unless the tactic also appears in refman_rst_tactics or has a worked example cited.
confidence_levels.summarized_semantics: Best-effort summary from papers/tutorials/changelog context, NOT a verbatim manual quote -- flagged wherever the manual's own prose could not be retrieved. Superseded by verified_verbatim_rst_source wherever both exist for the same tactic.
confidence_levels.changelog_only: Tactic/feature only known from a Releases changelog entry; behavior not independently described here.

$schema_notes.important_caveat: The new EasyCrypt/refman manual is still being written tactic-by-tactic (see r2026.02/r2026.03 '[documentation]: document the X tactic' changelog entries). As of this session refman/_sources/tactics/ contains at least: async-while, bindings, cfold, circuit, clear, extens, hint-simplify, hoare-split, if, proc, procstar, rnd, simplify-if, skip, splitwhile, swap (all captured below in refman_rst_tactics) -- but not yet e.g. wp, sp, seq, call, inline, conseq, sim, fel, transitivity, byequiv/byphoare/bypr, eager, kill, alias, fission/fusion, unroll, rcondt/rcondf, ring/field (these remain at verified_grammar/summarized_semantics confidence via ec-tactics/changelog). Re-check refman/_sources/tactics/ periodically for newly-added files.
$schema_notes.tooling_notes_for_future_sessions: Per explicit user instruction: when both a source file (.tex, .rst, grammar file) and a compiled artifact (PDF, rendered HTML) exist for the same content, fetch the SOURCE first and treat it as authoritative. Practical findings from this session: (1) GitHub blob pages for source files (.tex, .rst.txt) fetch cleanly once their exact URL is known -- either given directly by the user, or surfaced via web_search snippet -- but GitHub directory-tree pages (.../tree/...) are blocked by robots.txt, so a repo's file list cannot be browsed directly; filenames must be discovered externally. (2) The new refman's source tree keeps one .rst file per tactic under refman/_sources/tactics/<name>.rst.txt (the raw Sphinx source mirror published alongside the rendered HTML) -- this is the single best source for any tactic once its filename is known or guessable. (3) The compiled refman.pdf reliably fetches as text but this tool's PDF-to-text extraction consistently truncates at the same relative offset (partway through Section 3.3.5, before Section 3.4/Program Logics) regardless of text_content_token_limit or which PDF mirror is used -- treat the PDF as a source of last resort, not a reliable way to reach later chapters. (4) www.easycrypt.info (non-github.com) pages are not robots-blocked and were useful when GitHub paths were unknown.
$schema_notes.easycrypt_version_scheme: Since April 2022 EasyCrypt has used a stable rolling-release scheme tagged rYYYY.MM (e.g. r2022.04, r2025.11, r2026.07). Before r2022.04 there was no formal stable-release tagging; scripts/papers instead cite a git commit hash off the '1.0' branch (e.g. 'r2022.04-48-gc8d3d6c1'). r2022.04 is documented as 'First EasyCrypt stable release.'

ambient_logic.proof_engine_notes: Proofs manipulate a list of goals; each goal = (context: type variables + ordered assumptions) + (conclusion: one formula). Tactics reduce the first goal to zero or more subgoals. qed is only allowed once the goal list is empty.

tactics.name: idtac
tactics.description: Does nothing; leaves the goal unchanged.

tactics.name: move
tactics.description: Equivalent to idtac; used mainly with the introduction/generalization tacticals (move=> ..., move: ...).

tactics.name: clear
tactics.description: Removes assumptions a1..an from the context. Fails if a remaining assumption depends on one being cleared. Superseded/extended -- see refman_rst_tactics.clear for the current, richer opt-in/opt-out syntax.

tactics.name: assumption
tactics.description: Solves the goal if some context hypothesis is convertible to the conclusion.

tactics.name: reflexivity
tactics.description: Solves goals of the form b = b, up to computation (conversion).

tactics.name: left / right
tactics.description: Reduce a disjunctive goal to its left/right disjunct. For the classical `||`, right instead yields !phi1 => phi2 (differs from `\/`).

tactics.name: exists
tactics.description: Reduces an existential goal to a goal about the witness e satisfying the existential body.

tactics.name: split
tactics.description: Splits a conjunctive-shaped goal: <=> into both implications; /\ or && into two subgoals; equality of n-tuples into componentwise equalities. split * / split + (added r2026.06) iterate over top-level conjunctions.

tactics.name: congr
tactics.description: From f t1...tn = f u1...un produces subgoals ti = ui. congr pat / congr * variants added r2026.06.

tactics.name: subst
tactics.description: subst x: finds x = t (or t = x), substitutes everywhere, clears it. Bare subst repeats for all eligible identifiers.

tactics.name: trivial / done
tactics.description: trivial attempts to close the goal via low-level tactics (backs the // introduction pattern); done is trivial that fails if not closed.

tactics.name: simplify
tactics.syntax: simplify | simplify x1...xn | simplify delta | simplify hint ...
tactics.description: Reduces to beta/iota/zeta/logic head-normal form, plus optional delta-reduction. Gained a `hint` clause (named/local simplification-rule databases) in r2026.07 -- see refman_rst_tactics['hint simplify / hint / with hint'].

tactics.name: progress
tactics.description: Repeatedly applies split, subst, move=> to decompose the goal; tau (if given) is tried after each step.

tactics.name: smt
tactics.description: Sends the goal plus selected hypotheses/lemmas to SMT solvers. Options: timeout=, maxprovers=, prover=[...], axiom-selection controls. By default smt failures cannot be caught by try (strict mode).

tactics.name: admit
tactics.description: Closes the goal by admitting it (unsound).

tactics.name: change
tactics.description: Replaces the conclusion by phi, which must be convertible to it.

tactics.name: pose
tactics.description: Introduces a local definition for the first subterm matching pattern pi, abstracting its occurrences.

tactics.name: have / cut
tactics.description: Logical cut, producing a subgoal for phi and one for phi => original conclusion.

tactics.name: apply / exact
tactics.syntax: apply p | apply p in H | exact p
tactics.description: apply matches a proof term's conclusion against the goal; exact is apply followed by trivial.

tactics.name: rewrite
tactics.description: Rewrites using equational proof terms or operator-unfold patterns, with direction/occurrence/repetition modifiers. Extended to work in program-logic preconditions in r2026.03.

tactics.name: case / elim
tactics.description: case destructs the top assumption or does excluded-middle split on phi; elim additionally applies real induction for datatypes/integers.

tactics.name: algebra
tactics.description: Ring/field-style automated reasoning; the source manual leaves this as an undocumented placeholder.

tacticals.name: sequencing / branching
tacticals.description: Apply tau2 to all subgoals of tau1, or branch per-subgoal.

tacticals.name: try
tacticals.description: Runs tau, leaving the goal unchanged if it fails. smt failures cannot be caught by try in strict mode.

tacticals.name: do
tacticals.description: Repeats tau; exact stop conditions were not confirmable (source text truncated identically across every fetch attempt).

apply tac and require ALL resulting goals to be closed
combinators.try tac: try tac, ignore failure (already in tacticals)
combinators.do tac | do N tac: repeat (bare tacticals.do entry notes the exact stop condition was not independently confirmable from the manual source; CLAUDE.md confirms a counted form `do N tac` exists alongside bare `do tac`)
combinators.[tac1 | tac2 | ...]: apply a different tactic to each subgoal (matches the branching tactical already listed)
apply tac, then try trivial on the generated subgoals (introduction-pattern chaining, '//' = trivial)

refman_rst_tactics.note: Kept concise: syntax + core semantics + version note. Full worked Hoare/pHoare/pRHL/eHL examples live in the cited .rst.txt files.

proc.semantics: First tactic on a procedure-named goal. Concrete: unfolds call(s) into body/bodies. Abstract, non-relational: {formulaI} is an invariant over untouched globals; obligations that it holds initially, implies the postcondition, and is preserved by every module-argument procedure (phoare additionally forces bound=1 plus a losslessness obligation). Abstract, relational (both sides same abstract procedure): {formulaI} is a two-sided invariant; optional {formulaB} (bad event on the right) and {formulaJ} (invariant after it) let the sides desynchronize once {formulaB} occurs, adding a losslessness obligation.
proc.version_note: Documented r2026.03 (#884); abstract-phoare-proc's bound tightened to >=1 in r2026.03 (#887); an up-to-bad-specific variant added r2026.07 (#1060).

proc*.semantics: For relational goals where one procedure is abstract and the other concrete (no proc variant fits): replaces each procedure with a call statement, enabling e.g. inline on the concrete side.

clear.semantics: Bare clear removes everything not transitively used by the goal. clear -{idents} keeps only the named identifiers (opt-out). clear {idents} removes exactly those named, erroring if one is still depended upon (opt-in).
clear.version_note: Opt-out ('clear all unused') form added r2025.03 (#713); documented r2026.03 (#895).

rnd.semantics: Consumes a trailing `x <$ d`. HL: possibilistic weakest precondition (quantify over all sampled values). pHL: wp w.r.t. an event E (explicit or inferred), exact or bounded. pRHL two-sided: f,g form an isomorphism between the two distributions (g defaults to f; f defaults to identity) -- couples the samplings. pRHL {side}: consumes one side's sampling, requiring it lossless and the postcondition for every value. eHL: postcondition becomes its expectation over the sampled distribution.

skip.semantics: Applies to empty-program goals, reducing to a pure logical obligation (not discharged by skip itself). HL: pre implies post. pRHL: same, both sides empty. pHL: also requires weight 1%r to satisfy the stated bound. eHL: requires post-expectation bounded above by pre-expectation.
skip.version_note: No version-specific change beyond first documentation.

if.semantics: Case-splits a leading if-statement (must be first statement; use seq/sp first otherwise). HL: two subgoals per branch. pRHL bare if: lock-step -- proves the two guards agree under the invariant, then splits synchronized. pRHL if{side}: one-sided, splits only the named program's conditional. pHL: like HL (guard resolved with probability 1). eHL: like HL but the pre-expectation is additionally guarded by the branch condition/negation.

hoare split.semantics: Hoare-logic-ONLY: splits a goal whose postcondition is a top-level conjunction into one Hoare subgoal per conjunct; program/precondition untouched. Splits only the outermost conjunction (repeat for nested ones). Explicitly unsound to generalize to probabilistic/relational logics.
hoare split.version_note: Brand-new r2026.03 (#888); manual marks it 'new and subject to change'.

swap.semantics: Commutes independent (disjoint read/write) statements. Bare form swaps two adjacent commands; offset form swaps a command with one at a relative (n/-n) or absolute (@codepos1) position; range form swaps a contiguous block with commands at another position. Fails if the fragments actually depend on each other.
swap.version_note: Reworked r2025.02 to accept generalized/deep code positions (#650); guard against swapping past exception-raises added r2026.03 (#927); documented r2026.02 (#889).

cfold.semantics: Constant/copy-propagates an assignment `a <- b;` forward into later uses of a, rewriting the program (goal unchanged) with the assignment's effect preserved only at the region's end. {codepos} = start; optional {n} caps how many lines it propagates through.
cfold.version_note: Extended to symbolic assignments r2026.03 (#892); gained an 'eager' propagation mode r2026.05 (#938, fix #963).

splitwhile.semantics: Rewrites `while (b) { c }` into `while (b /\ S) { c }; while (b) { c }` for a user-given splitting condition S, letting an initial S-phase be reasoned about separately. S is never inferred. Logic-agnostic pure rewrite.

simplify if.semantics: If-conversion: rewrites an if-statement with pure-assignment branches into one conditional-expression assignment. Prevents wp's case-split from blowing up exponentially across many sequential ifs. With {codepos} (position selectors like ^if, ^if{2}, ^if{-2}) targets one if; bare form repeats everywhere applicable.

async while.semantics: pRHL-only `while` variant for loops NOT run in lockstep. L1/L2 mark lockstep vs one-side-only zones; k1/k2 are unrolling depths with f1/f2 the corresponding unrolling conditions. Generates goals: invariant/guard correspondence, HL preservation of I per side under its L, phoare termination of each raw loop, and I implies pre=>post at exit.
async while.version_note: Obligations fixed and documented r2026.05 (#935); underlying rule fixed earlier r2025.08 (#776).

circuit.syntax: circuit | circuit simplify | proc change circuit [bindings]? {codepos1}+{N} { stmt }
circuit.semantics: Discharges (or, 'simplify' mode, only rewrites) finite/bitstring-type goals by translating to boolean circuits. FOL: checks tautology directly. Hoare: translates pre/program/post to circuits, checks post implied by pre. equiv: one circuit map per program, checks the relational post. `circuit simplify` rewrites the postcondition via derived bit-level equalities without closing the goal. `proc change circuit` replaces a contiguous code block using the same circuit-equivalence check, automatically (no separate obligation), considering only variables live at the region's end. Requires every type/operator to be registered via `bind`; control flow, calls, sampling inside the region are unsupported (unroll/inline first).

extens.semantics: Extensionality case-split tactical: enumerates concrete values of a finite quantity, runs the given tactic per subgoal. Shape 1: `all P (iota_ start len)` over int -> one subgoal per integer in range. Shape 2: Hoare triple with binder [v] naming a bind-bitstring-bound variable -> 2^n subgoals (n=bit size) with v replaced by each concrete value throughout program/pre/post. Most useful with `circuit`/`circuit simplify` as the inner tactic (fixing one input often unblocks circuit translation); 2^n blow-up limits it to small bit-widths.

bind.syntax: bind bitstring to_bits from_bits to_uint to_sint of_int type size | bind array get set tolist oflist type size | bind op type op "name" | bind op [type1 & type2 & ...] op "name" | bind circuit op1 <- "name1", ... from "file"
bind.semantics: Command family (not a tactic) registering EasyCrypt types/operators against the circuit representation used by circuit/extens. bind bitstring: fixed-size bitstring isomorphism with bool list + signed/unsigned readings (7 side conditions). bind array: fixed-size array via get/set + list isomorphism (6 side conditions). bind op: operator implements one of a fixed bitvector/array-primitive catalog (arithmetic, bitwise, shifts, comparisons, extend/truncate/concat, indexing, array ops); monomorphic or multi-type form. bind circuit: asserts an operator equals an externally-specified circuit with NO generated proof obligation -- trusted, enters the TCB; prefer bind op when possible.

hint simplify / hint / with hint.syntax: hint simplify {lemma}+ | hint simplify in {db} : {lemma}+ | simplify hint {db}* {item}* | hint {db}* {item}* | hint clear {db}? | hint clear default | with hint {clause} ({tactic})
hint simplify / hint / with hint.semantics: Manages named databases of user reduction rules for simplify/cbv. Theory-level hint simplify [in db :] adds lemmas. The hint clause on simplify/cbv selects databases (unsigned = replace; +db/-db = add/remove) and can inline lemmas ({lemma...}) or restrict to operators (+[op...]/-[op...]). Standalone hint sets a persistent proof-local default (subgoal-branching applies); hint clear resets it. with hint {clause} (tactic) runs one tactic under a temporary hint config, restoring the original after.

llm_cli_tool.source: CLAUDE.md, uploaded by the user (found in the `llm` folder of an EasyCrypt checkout) -- an LLM-agent guide for EasyCrypt's `llm` subcommand.
llm_cli_tool.description: `easycrypt llm [OPTIONS] FILE.ec` is a non-interactive, batch-compilation mode purpose-built for LLM-agent workflows: no progress bar, no .eco cache files.

options.-upto LINE | -upto LINE:COL: Compile up to (not including) the given location, print the current goal state to stdout, exit 0. Used to inspect proof state at a specific point without running the rest of the file -- key for incremental proof development.
options.-lastgoals: On failure, print the goal state as it was just before the failing command to stdout, then the error to stderr, and exit 1. Used to see what the failing tactic was supposed to prove.
options.(standard): Standard loader/prover options are also available: -I, -timeout, -p, etc.

output_conventions.no_active_proof: if goals are requested with no active proof, stdout contains exactly: 'No active proof.'

recommended_workflow: 2. Write the .ec file. For a large proof, write the skeleton with `admit`-ed subgoals first, then fill in detail.
3. Run `easycrypt llm -lastgoals FILE.ec`. Exit 0 = done. Exit 1 = read the stderr error and the stdout goal state to see what went wrong.
4. Use `-upto LINE` to inspect the proof state at a specific point without running the rest of the file (incremental development).
5. Fix and repeat from step 2. The final proof should contain no `admit`/`admitted`.
guidelines_from_claude_md: Use the SMT solver only in direct mode (smt() or /#) on simple goals (arithmetic, pure logical goals).
Refrain from unfolding operator definitions unless necessary; if more properties on an operator are needed, state them as a dedicated lemma rather than unfolding definitions in higher-level proofs.
